title: Attention throughput saturation matrix and microprofiling notes
content:
Summary:

This note documents a targeted microprofiling run to build a saturation matrix for attention kernel variants we depend on in the runtime: FlashAttention(v1/v2), paged attention (paged KV caching pathway), and a few fused-op kernels we prototype (QKV concat + fused softmax + dropout). The goal is to map utilization/throughput regimes across the common workload dimensions (sequence length, effective batch, kv-cache hit rate, precision/quantization) and to surface non-obvious bottlenecks (kernel launch overhead, memory-bound stages, divergence in tiled kernels).

Why this: we have intermittent throughput cliffs under real traffic (small bursts, long-context queries) where total tokens/sec drops disproportionally. Hypothesis: different kernels hit distinct saturation points; sometimes the runtime routing picks a kernel that is suboptimal for the current sequence-length distribution. This matrix will help us:
- Define safe routing boundaries (seq/batch thresholds)
- Tune autoscaling and batching heuristics
- Guide fused-op rollout and fallbacks

Hardware + stack details used for experiments:
- Machine: g4dn-like equivalent (A100-40GB emulation in perf lab), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN latest, Nsight Systems 2024.3 for traces
- Binary: runtime branch feature/attn-saturation-matrix @ commit 9f2c3e (linked PR above)
- Models: llama2-13b (FP16, KV cache enabled), codegen-6b (FP16), small 1.4B internal test model (FP32 baseline)
- Kernels evaluated: FlashAttention-v2 (FA2), FlashAttention-v1 (FA1), paged-attn (paged), fused-qkv-softmax (fused), fallback-cuda-gemm (fallback)
- Measurement tooling: token throughput measured from runtime metrics (tokens/s), latency p50/p95/p99 from trace events, GPU metrics via nvprof/Nsight (SM utilization, achieved occupancy, tensor core utilization, DRAM BW).

Experiment matrix (canonical grid):
- Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512, 2048
- Effective batch sizes (tokens per step / parallel requests): 1, 4, 16, 64
- KV-cache hit rates: 0% (cold), 50% partial reuse, 100% warm (full reuse)
- Precision: FP32, FP16, int8-quant (simulated by quantized kernel where available)
- Kernel variant: FA2, FA1, paged, fused, fallback

Short summary of surprising findings (high level):
1) Micro-batch cliff at small batches and mid-long sequences: for batch=1 and seq>=512 FA2 throughput collapses ~2.2x vs batch=4. Root cause: kernel launch latency and small matrix shapes cause low SM occupancy combined with token serialization inside fused staging.
2) Paged attention shines at long contexts when cache hit >=50%: paged-attn shows ~1.6x higher tokens/s vs FA2 at seq=2048 with warm cache because it reduces upstream memory copies and avoids recomputing KV projection loads across layers.
3) Fused op instability at high occupancy: our fused-qkv-softmax kernel saturates DRAM BW at larger batches (>=16) causing the downstream softmax to become memory-bound; perf is worse than unaffiliated FA2 for batch>=64
4) FA1 sometimes wins on short sequences and tiny batches because its lower kernel setup overhead and simpler tiling matches these shapes better than FA2's heavier precomputation.
5) p99 tail driven by micro-serialization in our runtime queueing when switching kernel types between requests. The kernel choice change introduces ~0.8–1.5 ms additional tail due to rebinds.

Representative numbers (single A100-like node, tokens/sec):
- Model: llama2-13b FP16, seq=512, batch=1, KV=warm:
  - FA2: 1,150 tok/s (p50 7.8ms, p99 24.1ms)
  - FA1: 2,400 tok/s (p50 3.9ms, p99 12.5ms)
  - paged: 1,850 tok/s (p50 5.2ms, p99 15.8ms)
  - fused: 1,020 tok/s (p50 8.6ms, p99 27.9ms)
- Model: llama2-13b FP16, seq=2048, batch=16, KV=warm:
  - FA2: 24,500 tok/s (p50 1.9ms per request equivalent, p99 6.4ms)
  - paged: 38,700 tok/s (p50 1.2ms, p99 3.1ms)
  - fused: 30,200 tok/s (p50 1.4ms, p99 4.3ms)

Profiling artifacts and explanations:
- Nsight flame graphs for the long-seq/paged run show 40% less memory-copy time in the host->device stage; paged-attn uses a persistent region for layer KV when cache hits are high.
- CUPTI kernel summaries indicate FA2 emits more small kernels (~3x) of shorter duration compared to FA1 for seq<=128; this increases relative kernel launch overhead.
- DRAM BW traces show fused kernel runs reaching 85–92% of sustained DRAM BW in high-batch regimes—this explains why fused loses headroom for higher batch sizes.

Hypotheses validated / rejected:
- Hypothesis: quantized (int8) kernels always increase throughput. Outcome: partially true for very large batches and short contexts; but for long-context queries the quantized path causes extra dequantize/convert overheads that cancel the wins.
- Hypothesis: pipeline stall due to KV copy is the main tail source. Outcome: partially true, but runtime kernel-switch rebind overhead was an equal contributor to p99 tails in mixed-traffic traces.

Immediate recommendations for runtime changes:
1) Add a lightweight kernel-selection heuristic: prefer FA1 for batch<=2 and seq<=512; prefer paged-attn when seq>=1024 and measured cache hit>60%; prefer fused only when batch in [8,32] and DRAM BW headroom confirmed.
2) Add a fast-path to avoid kernel rebind on kernel family changes within a short time window (e.g., 200ms) to reduce p99. Rebinds should be lazy and amortized across a few requests.
3) Expose a per-model recommended default routing table based on an automated offline saturation matcher (we can populate from this matrix).
4) Avoid fused rollout to production for batch>=64 until we optimize memory layout to reduce DRAM BW pressure.

Notes on experimental methodology caveats:
- Our perf lab A100-like hardware has different DRAM BW characteristics than TPU/GPU fleet variants; absolute numbers should not be used for SLAs. Use relative deltas.
- The runtime instrumentation (timers and tracing) can add ~1–2% overhead on short runs; we used sampling and repeated runs to stabilize numbers.
- Mixed workloads in production (varying seq/batch) show non-linear effects not captured in a per-shape matrix; we will run a second phase with synthetic mixed-traffic to validate heuristics.

Action items and next steps:
- (Ethan) Implement selection heuristic prototype in branch feature/attn-routing-hints (ETA: 2w). Link: PR above.
- (Marisol) Reproduce fused kernel DRAM BW pressure with microbench that varies memory layout (ETA: 1w).
- (Jonah) Setup mixed-traffic validator harness and run overnight with production-like distribution (ETA: 3 days).
- (Aisha) Collate saturation matrix into a CSV and push to gs://redwood-artifacts/attn-matrix/2024-10- (TODO to name) and add to linked_artifacts.

Useful commands / quick runbook (internal):
- run target shape: ./run_profile.sh --model llama2-13b --seq 512 --batch 1 --kernel fa2 --iters 2000 --warmup 300 --out trace_fa2_512_b1.json
- nv-nsight capture: nsight-sys -o profile_fa2_512_b1.qs -- ./bin/serve --profile-target trace_fa2_512_b1.json
- extract kernel summary: python tools/parse_nsight.py profile_fa2_512_b1.qs > profile_fa2_512_b1.summary

Open questions we need to answer in phase 2:
- Can we make fused kernel memory accesses more cache-friendly (change layout to AoS vs SoA) without breaking other models?
- At what cache hit % threshold does paged-attn always trump FA2 across models? (empirically ~55–65% now, need more data)
- Is there a low-overhead way to detect and batch small incoming requests to avoid FA2 small-batch penalty?

Appendix: short run logs (trimmed)
- run: seq=512 batch=1 fa2
  avg_tok_s: 1150, p50_ms: 7.8, p99_ms: 24.1, sm_util: 31%, dram_bw: 145 GB/s
- run: seq=512 batch=1 fa1
  avg_tok_s: 2400, p50_ms: 3.9, p99_ms: 12.5, sm_util: 48%, dram_bw: 98 GB/s
- run: seq=2048 batch=16 paged
  avg_tok_s: 38700, p50_ms: 1.2, p99_ms: 3.1, sm_util: 82%, dram_bw: 160 GB/s

If this looks good I will convert the matrix to CSV and upload artifacts, and start wiring the heuristic into the runtime. Comments and corrections welcome — especially from anyone who has profiled FA1/FA2 on the fleet GPUs (differences in DRAM BW and kernel-launch penalty might change thresholds).
